Add ElastiCache in front of the database using lazy loading for product queries
Convert the database to a Multi-AZ deployment and send reads to the standby
Use Route 53 geolocation routing to the single Region
questions.explanation: Edge caching serves repeated GETs close to users and keeps them away from the origin. An in-memory cache absorbs repeated database reads. A Multi-AZ standby instance is not readable, and DNS routing to one Region does not cut distance.
rationales: Correct: edge caching cuts latency and origin load.
Correct: cache hits avoid database queries.
An RDS Multi-AZ instance standby does not serve reads.
There is only one Region, so routing does not reduce latency.

sources.title: What is Amazon CloudFront — CloudFront docs
Caching strategies — ElastiCache docs

questions.stem:
A database on EC2 needs 12,000 IOPS on a 300 GiB EBS volume. The current gp2 volume would need to be much larger than 300 GiB to reach that IOPS level.

What is the most cost-effective change?
options: Move to a gp3 volume and provision 12,000 IOPS independently of size
Grow the gp2 volume until its baseline IOPS reaches 12,000
Use an st1 throughput-optimized HDD volume
Stripe several instance store volumes
questions.explanation: gp2 IOPS scale with volume size, so you would pay for capacity you do not need. gp3 lets you provision IOPS and throughput separately from size, usually at a lower price per GiB.
rationales: Correct: IOPS independent of size.
Pays for unneeded capacity.
HDD volumes suit sequential throughput, not random database IOPS.
Instance store is ephemeral and loses data when the instance stops.

sources.title: General purpose SSD volumes — EBS docs

questions.stem:
A company runs a three-tier web application on EC2 in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Twice last month customers reported the checkout page failing for 20 minutes before the operations team noticed. All CPU and ALB health-check alarms stayed green during both incidents.

Which change gives the earliest detection of this kind of failure with the least custom code?
options: Turn on CloudTrail data events for the application's S3 buckets.
Enable detailed (1-minute) EC2 monitoring on all instances.
Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that run the checkout journey on a schedule, and alarm on canary failures.
Lower the CPU alarm threshold on the Auto Scaling group from 70% to 40%.
questions.explanation: The failures were functional, and every infrastructure metric stayed healthy. Outside-in synthetic monitoring runs the real user path on a schedule and alarms when it fails, which closes the gap between infrastructure health and user experience.
rationales: CloudTrail records API activity for audit. It is not a functional availability monitor.
Finer-grained resource metrics still do not show that checkout is functionally broken.
Correct. Canaries test the user journey from outside, so they catch functional failures that resource metrics and shallow health checks miss.
CPU was normal during the incidents. A lower threshold only adds noise.

sources.title: Synthetic monitoring — CloudWatch docs

questions.stem:
A platform team receives about 300 alarm notifications a week. Most come from a single database slowdown that triggers latency, CPU, queue-depth and error-rate alarms on several services at once. On-call engineers have started ignoring pages.

Which approach most directly reduces noise while keeping the pages actionable?
options: Create CloudWatch composite alarms that page only when a meaningful combination of underlying alarms is in ALARM, and set the individual alarms to not notify.
Send all alarms to an SQS queue and have engineers poll it hourly.
Increase every alarm's evaluation period to 30 minutes.
Delete the CPU and queue-depth alarms and keep only error-rate alarms.
questions.explanation: Composite alarms combine alarm states with Boolean logic, so one page represents the incident. The underlying alarms stay available for diagnosis without each one sending a notification.
rationales: Correct. Composite alarms collapse correlated symptoms into one actionable page.
This hides incidents and slows response.
This delays detection of real incidents and does not remove duplicate pages.
Losing diagnostic signals hurts troubleshooting. The noise problem is notification design, not signal collection.

sources.title: Composite alarms — CloudWatch docs

questions.stem:
An organization has 40 workload accounts managed with AWS Organizations. Developers troubleshooting a request that crosses services in four accounts have to sign in to each account separately to see metrics, logs and X-Ray traces. Security does not want to create IAM users in workload accounts.

What should a solutions architect recommend?
options: Set up CloudWatch cross-account observability, with a central monitoring account linked to the workload source accounts.
Create IAM users for each developer in every workload account and share a password vault.
Enable an organization trail in CloudTrail and query it with Athena.
Copy all CloudWatch metrics nightly to a central S3 bucket with a Lambda function.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch cross-account observability links source accounts to a monitoring account. Engineers can then search and correlate metrics, logs and traces across accounts from one console without per-account credentials.
rationales: Correct. This gives a single place to view metrics, logs and traces across linked accounts.
This is the anti-pattern security wants to avoid, and it still requires switching accounts.
CloudTrail shows API calls, not application metrics, logs or traces.
This is custom, delayed and leaves out traces and interactive troubleshooting.

sources.title: Cross-account observability — CloudWatch docs

questions.stem:
A microservices application on Amazon ECS shows p99 latency rising from 300 ms to 2 s after a release. Each of the 12 services reports normal CPU and memory.

Which tool should the team adopt to find the service responsible?
options: Instrument the services with AWS X-Ray (or AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry) and analyse the trace service map and segment timings.
Increase task CPU and memory for all services.
Enable VPC Flow Logs on the ECS subnets.
Turn on AWS Config recording for all ECS resources.
questions.explanation: When resource metrics are normal but end-to-end latency degrades, distributed tracing is the right tool. It breaks each request into segments per service and downstream call, showing where the time goes.
rationales: Correct. Distributed tracing shows time spent per hop and pinpoints the slow dependency.
Resources are not saturated, so scaling blindly wastes money and may not help.
Flow logs show IP traffic metadata, not per-request application latency.
Config tracks configuration changes, not request latency.

sources.title: What is AWS X-Ray — X-Ray docs

questions.stem:
Operators restart a hung application service on EC2 instances by hand whenever a specific CloudWatch alarm fires. This often happens at night and response takes 30-60 minutes.

Which solution automates the response with the least operational overhead?
options: Configure the Auto Scaling group to replace every instance nightly.
Run a cron job on a dedicated EC2 "ops" instance that SSHs into each server every 5 minutes and restarts the service.
Use an EventBridge rule on the alarm state change to start a Systems Manager Automation runbook that restarts the service on the affected instance.
Page a second on-call engineer so two people respond.
questions.explanation: An EventBridge rule can match a CloudWatch alarm state change and invoke a Systems Manager Automation runbook. That turns a manual runbook into an audited, repeatable action without managing extra infrastructure.
rationales: It does not respond to the actual event and can disrupt users.
This creates a new single point of failure, needs SSH keys, and restarts healthy services needlessly.
Correct. This is managed, auditable, event-driven remediation with no servers to run.
This does not automate anything.

sources.title: What is Amazon EventBridge — EventBridge docs
Systems Manager Automation — Systems Manager docs

questions.stem:
A security review finds that administrators reach private EC2 instances through a bastion host whose security group allows SSH (port 22) from 0.0.0.0/0. SSH keys are shared among the team, and there is no record of commands run.

Which remediation improves security the most while keeping administrative access?
options: Move the bastion to a private subnet and keep port 22 open to 0.0.0.0/0.
Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager with IAM-based access and session logging, then remove the bastion and close inbound port 22.
Enable GuardDuty to detect SSH brute-force attempts against the bastion.
Restrict the bastion security group to the office IP range and rotate the shared key quarterly.
questions.explanation: Session Manager provides interactive access controlled by IAM, with no inbound ports or SSH keys. Sessions can be logged to S3 or CloudWatch Logs, so it fixes the exposure and the audit gap together.
rationales: Administrators can no longer reach it, and the over-broad rule stays.
Correct. This removes the open port and shared keys and adds auditing.
Detection does not remove the exposure.
This is an improvement, but keys are still shared and sessions are still not logged.

sources.title: Session Manager — Systems Manager docs

questions.stem:
A company manages 1,200 EC2 instances across 30 accounts in AWS Organizations. Auditors require proof that critical OS patches are applied within 14 days. Each team patches today with its own scripts, and there is no central report.

Which approach meets the requirement with the least operational effort?
options: Enable Amazon Inspector and email findings to each team.
Use Systems Manager Patch Manager with patch baselines and maintenance windows deployed through an organization-wide patch policy, and report compliance centrally.
Use AWS Config to record instance configuration changes.
Build new golden AMIs monthly and ask teams to redeploy when convenient.
questions.explanation: Patch Manager defines approved patches with baselines and applies them in maintenance windows. Organization-wide patch policies extend this across accounts, with central compliance reporting as audit evidence.
rationales: Inspector finds vulnerabilities but does not apply patches or enforce a schedule.
Correct. This gives managed, scheduled patching with compliance reporting across accounts.
Config records configuration but does not patch.
It does not enforce the 14-day window or report compliance.

sources.title: Patch Manager — Systems Manager docs

questions.stem:
Engineers frequently change security group rules in the console on resources that were deployed with AWS CloudFormation. Later stack updates fail or silently revert those changes, which causes outages.

Which actions together address the root cause? (Select two.)
options: Run CloudFormation drift detection regularly and fold intended changes back into the templates.
Enable termination protection on all stacks.
Delete and recreate every stack weekly.
Increase the stack update timeout.
Remove console write permissions for stack-managed resources and route changes through the IaC pipeline.
questions.explanation: Drift detection finds out-of-band changes, so they can be folded back into templates. Limiting manual change permissions keeps all future changes going through the pipeline. Together they keep IaC authoritative.
rationales: Correct. It shows where reality diverges from the template, so the template stays the source of truth.
It only prevents stack deletion, not drift.
This is disruptive and does not stop console changes.
Timeouts are unrelated to configuration drift.
Correct. This prevents new out-of-band changes.

sources.title: Detect drift on stacks — CloudFormation docs

questions.stem:
A company must make sure that no security group in its AWS accounts allows unrestricted inbound SSH. Violations should be corrected within minutes without human action, and an audit history must be kept.

Which solution meets these requirements?
options: Enable VPC Flow Logs and alert on traffic to port 22.
Use an SCP that denies ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress for all principals.
Have a Lambda function scan all security groups once a week and email the results.
Deploy an AWS Config managed rule for unrestricted SSH with an automatic remediation action that runs a Systems Manager Automation document to remove the rule.
questions.explanation: AWS Config evaluates resources continuously and records compliance history. Remediation actions attach SSM Automation documents that can run automatically, so non-compliant rules are corrected without human action.
rationales: This detects traffic, not the misconfiguration, and does not remediate.
This blocks all ingress changes, which breaks legitimate operations.
Weekly and manual: it does not meet the minutes requirement.
Correct. This gives continuous evaluation, automatic remediation and a compliance history.

sources.title: Remediating resources — AWS Config docs

questions.stem:
GuardDuty in a production account reports that an EC2 instance is talking to a known cryptocurrency-mining pool. The security team wants an automated response that stops the threat and keeps the ability to investigate.

Which automated response is most appropriate?
options: An EventBridge rule invokes a Lambda function that terminates the instance immediately.

An EventBridge rule for the finding type invokes a Step Functions workflow that swaps the instance's security groups for an isolation group with no rules, snapshots its EBS volumes, tags it and notifies the security team.
Reboot the instance with a Systems Manager Run Command.
Suppress the finding type in GuardDuty to avoid alert fatigue.
questions.explanation: GuardDuty findings are emitted to EventBridge, where they can trigger orchestrated responses. The best practice is to isolate the instance and capture snapshots so the investigation can go ahead, rather than destroying it.
rationales: Termination destroys memory and disk evidence needed for forensics.
Correct. It contains the threat and preserves evidence.
Rebooting may clear evidence and may not stop a persistent miner.
This ignores an active compromise.

sources.title: What is Amazon EventBridge — EventBridge docs
GuardDuty with Organizations — GuardDuty docs

questions.stem:
A company has enabled security services in 60 accounts across three Regions. Analysts sign in to each account to review findings, and new accounts are often missed for weeks.

What should a solutions architect do to improve this?
options: Export findings from each account to CSV weekly and merge them in a spreadsheet.
Use the organization management account as the place where analysts work every day.
Create one IAM user per analyst in every account.
Designate a delegated administrator account for the security services through AWS Organizations, enable auto-enable for new member accounts, and aggregate findings across Regions.
questions.explanation: AWS security services integrate with Organizations through a delegated administrator. That account sees findings for all members, can auto-enable new accounts, and can aggregate Regions, which removes the per-account review burden.
rationales: This is manual, delayed and error-prone.
AWS recommends keeping day-to-day workloads and access out of the management account.
Credential sprawl that does not solve aggregation.
Correct. This gives central visibility and automatic coverage of new accounts.

sources.title: GuardDuty with Organizations — GuardDuty docs
What is Security Hub — Security Hub docs

questions.stem:
After December 2025, a security architect is updating a design document. The current design uses "Security Hub" to run the CIS and AWS Foundational Security Best Practices standards and to collect findings in ASFF. Leadership also wants correlated, risk-prioritised exposures that combine GuardDuty, Inspector and Macie signals.

Which description of the target design is accurate?
options: Use Amazon Inspector as the central aggregator for all findings.
Security Hub has been retired; replace it with AWS Config alone.
Use Amazon Macie for CIS standards and GuardDuty for exposure correlation.
Use AWS Security Hub CSPM for the standards and posture checks, and the new AWS Security Hub to correlate findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Security Hub CSPM and Macie into prioritised exposures.
questions.explanation: AWS renamed the legacy posture service to Security Hub CSPM and launched a new Security Hub (GA December 2025) that correlates signals into exposures. Standards-based posture checks belong in Security Hub CSPM, and risk prioritisation belongs in the new Security Hub.
rationales: Inspector is a vulnerability scanner, not the aggregation and correlation layer.
Neither service has been retired, and Config does not provide exposure correlation.
This reverses the roles. Macie finds sensitive data and GuardDuty detects threats.
Correct. This matches the 2025 split of Security Hub into two services.

sources.title: Security Hub near-real-time analytics — What's New
Security Hub GA — AWS News Blog

questions.stem:
A Lambda function reads an RDS for PostgreSQL password from an encrypted environment variable. The password has not changed in three years. Compliance now requires credentials to be rotated every 30 days without redeploying code.

Which solution meets the requirement?
options: Use a KMS customer managed key with automatic key rotation for the environment variable.
Hard-code the password in a Lambda layer and update the layer monthly.
Rotate the password manually and update the environment variable every 30 days.
Store the credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation configured, and have the function retrieve the secret at runtime (with caching).
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores credentials and rotates them on a schedule. Applications fetch the current value at runtime, so rotation happens without code or configuration redeployment.
rationales: KMS key rotation changes the encryption key, not the database password.
Still embedded, and still requires redeployment.
Manual work that needs a configuration change and is error-prone.
Correct. Rotation is managed, and code changes are not needed for each rotation.

sources.title: Rotate secrets — Secrets Manager docs

questions.stem:
An internal audit finds that many IAM roles across a company's accounts carry broad permissions. Many of those permissions appear never to have been used. The company wants to move toward least privilege based on evidence, not guesswork.

Which actions should a solutions architect recommend? (Select two.)
options: Delete all roles not modified in the last 90 days.
Enable Amazon Macie on all S3 buckets.
Use IAM Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail activity to create tighter policies for active roles.
Enable IAM Access Analyzer unused access analysis to find unused roles, access keys and permissions.
Attach AdministratorAccess to all roles temporarily and log what breaks.
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer reports unused access and can generate policies from recorded CloudTrail activity. Together they shrink permissions to what workloads actually use.
rationales: Modification date says nothing about usage, and deleting roles could break workloads.
Macie classifies data. It does not analyse IAM permission usage.
Correct. It produces policies based on actual usage.
Correct. It gives evidence of which granted access is not exercised.
This widens risk, the opposite of least privilege.

sources.title: IAM Access Analyzer — IAM docs

questions.stem:
A company discovered that a developer briefly made an S3 bucket containing customer data public. The company wants to prevent public S3 access in all production accounts, and to make sure account administrators cannot turn the protection off.

Which combination best meets the requirement?
options: Enable S3 Block Public Access at the account level in each production account, and attach an SCP to the production OU that denies changes to the Block Public Access settings.
Enable Amazon Macie to find the sensitive data.
Add a bucket policy to every bucket that denies s3:GetObject to anonymous users.
Turn on S3 server access logging for all buckets.
questions.explanation: Account-level Block Public Access overrides bucket ACLs and policies that would grant public access. An SCP that denies changes to that setting makes sure administrators in member accounts cannot weaken it.
rationales: Correct. This prevents public access, and the SCP stops local administrators from undoing it.
Macie classifies data but does not prevent public access.
This must be maintained per bucket, and administrators can remove it.
Logging is detective only.

sources.title: S3 Block Public Access — S3 docs

questions.stem:
A company runs container images from Amazon ECR on Amazon ECS and serverless functions on AWS Lambda. Security wants continuous visibility into known software vulnerabilities in these workloads, including newly published CVEs that affect images already deployed.

Which service should be enabled?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor.
Amazon Macie.
Amazon Inspector, with scanning for ECR images and Lambda functions.
Amazon GuardDuty.
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector scans EC2 instances, ECR container images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities, and it re-evaluates them as new CVEs are published.
rationales: Trusted Advisor checks best practices; it does not scan software packages.
Macie discovers sensitive data in S3.
Correct. Inspector continuously scans ECR images and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities.
GuardDuty detects threats and suspicious behaviour, not CVEs in packages.

sources.title: What is Amazon Inspector — Inspector docs

questions.stem:
A reporting application on Amazon RDS for MySQL has a primary instance at 95% CPU during business hours. Performance analysis shows that about 85% of queries are reads, and many of them repeat the same dashboard aggregations. The team proposes moving to an instance class twice as large.

Which approach improves performance more cost-effectively? (Select two.)
options: Double the primary instance size as proposed.
Add one or more read replicas and route reporting reads to them.
Enable Multi-AZ on the primary to share the read load.
Switch storage from gp3 to magnetic volumes.
Cache repeated dashboard query results in Amazon ElastiCache.
questions.explanation: With most queries being repeated reads, offloading them to read replicas and caching hot results removes most load from the primary. This scales further and costs less than vertical scaling.
rationales: A costly vertical fix for a read-dominated load that will hit the next ceiling.
Correct. This offloads read traffic from the primary.
A classic Multi-AZ standby instance does not serve read traffic; it is for availability.
Magnetic storage is slower and does not address CPU.
Correct. Repeated aggregations are served from memory, which removes load.

sources.title: RDS read replicas — RDS docs
Caching strategies — ElastiCache docs

questions.stem:
After moving an API to AWS Lambda, a team sees "too many connections" errors on its Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster during traffic bursts, even though database CPU stays low.

What is the most effective improvement?
options: Increase the Aurora instance size to raise max_connections.
Move the functions into a VPC with more subnets.
Raise the Lambda reserved concurrency so bursts finish faster.
Place Amazon RDS Proxy between the Lambda functions and the Aurora cluster to pool and reuse connections.
questions.explanation: Many short-lived Lambda invocations each open their own database connection. RDS Proxy pools and shares connections, which protects the database from connection storms without scaling the instance.
rationales: A costly workaround that does not address connection churn.
Subnet count does not change database connection behaviour.
More concurrent functions open more connections, which makes the problem worse.
Correct. RDS Proxy multiplexes many function connections onto a smaller pool.

sources.title: Amazon RDS Proxy — RDS docs

questions.stem:
An e-commerce site has a sharp traffic ramp every weekday at 08:00. Instances take about 8 minutes to boot and warm caches. A target tracking policy on CPU reacts, but users see errors for the first 10 minutes of the ramp.

Which change addresses the problem most directly?
options: Add a predictive scaling policy, optionally with a warm pool of pre-initialised instances, so capacity is in place before the daily ramp.
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer.
Lower the target tracking CPU target from 50% to 20% all day.
Increase the health-check grace period.
questions.explanation: Reactive scaling cannot cover a long boot time on a sharp, predictable ramp. Predictive scaling learns the daily cycle and launches instances in advance, and warm pools shorten readiness further.
rationales: Correct. It forecasts the recurring pattern and launches capacity ahead of demand.
The load balancer type is not the bottleneck; instance readiness is.
This over-provisions all day and still reacts after the ramp starts.
This only delays health evaluation and does not add capacity sooner.

sources.title: Predictive scaling — EC2 Auto Scaling docs

questions.stem:
A VPC has private subnets in three Availability Zones. All of them route internet-bound traffic through a single NAT gateway in AZ-a. During an AZ-a impairment, workloads in AZ-b and AZ-c lost access to external APIs.

How should the architecture be improved?
options: Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance in AZ-a.
Add a second NAT gateway in AZ-a.
Deploy a NAT gateway in each AZ and update each AZ's private route table to use the NAT gateway in the same AZ.
Increase the NAT gateway bandwidth.
questions.explanation: A NAT gateway is zonal. Building one per AZ, with AZ-local routing, means an AZ failure only affects resources in that AZ.
rationales: Still a single AZ, with more operational burden.
Both gateways still share the failure domain of AZ-a.
Correct. This removes the cross-AZ dependency and also avoids cross-AZ data charges.
Bandwidth was not the problem; the AZ dependency was.

sources.title: NAT gateways — Amazon VPC docs

questions.stem:
When a downstream payment service recovers from a brief outage, it immediately fails again. Logs show thousands of clients retrying every 100 ms at exactly the same moments.

Which improvements should a solutions architect recommend? (Select two.)
options: Reduce client timeouts to 10 ms so retries happen faster.
Implement exponential backoff with jitter in the clients' retry logic.
Remove retries entirely.
Add a circuit breaker so clients stop calling the service while it is failing and probe it gradually.
Increase the retry count to 50.
questions.explanation: Synchronised retries create load spikes that knock over a recovering service. Exponential backoff with jitter spreads retries out, and a circuit breaker stops traffic until the dependency is healthy.
rationales: This adds more retries and makes the storm worse.
Correct. Retries are spread out over increasing intervals.
Transient failures then become user-facing errors.
Correct. This prevents overload while the service recovers.
More retries add load during recovery.

sources.title: Timeouts, retries and jitter — Builders Library

questions.stem:
A company documented RTO and RPO targets for 30 critical applications two years ago. Since then architectures have changed, and leadership doubts the targets are still achievable. The company wants an ongoing assessment plus evidence from real failure tests.

Which combination of services meets these needs?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor and AWS Budgets.
AWS Resilience Hub to assess applications against their RTO/RPO policies on an ongoing basis, and AWS Fault Injection Service to run controlled failure experiments.
Amazon Inspector and AWS Config.
AWS CloudTrail and Amazon Macie.
questions.explanation: Resilience Hub evaluates applications against defined RTO/RPO targets and recommends improvements over time. Fault Injection Service runs controlled experiments to show that recovery mechanisms actually work.
rationales: Neither assesses RTO/RPO or injects faults.
Correct. Assessment and validation through real fault injection.
Vulnerability and configuration compliance, not resilience validation.
Audit logging and data classification are unrelated to resilience.

sources.title: What is AWS Resilience Hub — Resilience Hub docs

questions.stem:
A company spends steadily on EC2 across several instance families in two Regions. Over the next three years it plans to move much of that workload to Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate and some to AWS Lambda.

Which commitment option preserves savings through the modernisation?
options: EC2 Instance Savings Plans for the current instance families.
Spot Instances for the entire workload.
Standard Reserved Instances for each instance type.
Compute Savings Plans.
questions.explanation: Compute Savings Plans apply to EC2 usage regardless of family, size, Region or OS, and also to Fargate and Lambda. The discount follows the workload as it modernises.
rationales: Tied to an instance family in a Region and do not apply to Fargate or Lambda.
Not a commitment, and unsuitable for steady, interruption-sensitive production workloads.
Inflexible and EC2-only, so they become stranded as the workload moves.
Correct. They apply across instance families and Regions and also cover Fargate and Lambda.

sources.title: What are Savings Plans — Savings Plans docs

questions.stem:
A company runs a stable fleet of memory-optimised instances from one instance family in a single Region. The usage is predictable for the next three years and will not change family or Region. Finance wants the largest discount from a Savings Plan.

Which option should be chosen?
options: A Compute Savings Plan.
On-Demand with Cost Anomaly Detection.
An EC2 Instance Savings Plan for that instance family in that Region.
A Spot Fleet with on-demand fallback.
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans give a deeper discount in return for committing to a specific family in a specific Region. When those will not change, the lost flexibility costs nothing.
rationales: More flexible, but the discount is generally smaller than an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the same commitment.
No discount.
Correct. It trades flexibility for a deeper discount, which suits a fixed fleet.
Unsuitable for steady production, and not a Savings Plan.

sources.title: What are Savings Plans — Savings Plans docs

questions.stem:
A company spends a steady amount on Amazon Aurora, Amazon RDS and Amazon DynamoDB across two Regions. It expects to change some database engines and instance families during the next year and wants commitment-based savings that remain applicable.

Which purchasing option best fits?
options: Compute Savings Plans.
Database Savings Plans.
EC2 Instance Savings Plans.
RDS Reserved Instances for each current DB instance class.
questions.explanation: Database Savings Plans, launched in December 2025, cover steady spend on supported database services such as Aurora, RDS and DynamoDB. The commitment stays flexible across engine, instance family and Region.
rationales: Apply to EC2, Fargate and Lambda, not managed database services.
Correct. A commitment model for supported database services that is flexible across engine, instance family and Region.
Apply only to EC2 instance usage.
Tied to specific configurations and does not cover DynamoDB.

questions.stem:
A media company runs nightly video-processing batch jobs on On-Demand EC2. The jobs are checkpointed, can be restarted and must finish within an 8-hour window. A previous Spot pilot on a single instance type suffered frequent interruptions.

Which change lowers cost while keeping the jobs reliable?
options: Buy a 3-year Compute Savings Plan sized to the nightly peak.
Run the jobs on Spot Instances diversified across many instance types and AZs, using the price-capacity-optimized allocation strategy, with a small On-Demand base.
Move the jobs to Dedicated Hosts.
Retry the Spot pilot on the same single instance type with a higher maximum price.
questions.explanation: Fault-tolerant, checkpointed batch work is a good fit for Spot. Diversifying across instance types and AZs, with the price-capacity-optimized strategy, draws from deeper capacity pools and lowers interruption rates.
rationales: Commits around the clock for an 8-hour-a-day workload.
Correct. Diversification and a capacity-aware allocation strategy reduce interruptions.
Costs more and is not needed for this workload.
A single capacity pool is still prone to interruption.

sources.title: Spot Instances — EC2 docs

questions.stem:
A data platform team stores several petabytes in S3 Standard. Some datasets are read heavily for weeks and then rarely; others are read unpredictably for years. The team cannot predict access per dataset.

Which storage approach minimises cost with the least operational effort?
options: Write a Lambda function that moves objects based on CloudTrail data events.
Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering for these datasets.
Create Lifecycle rules that move all objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
Move all data to S3 One Zone-IA.
questions.explanation: When access patterns are unknown or change over time, S3 Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers automatically based on access, without retrieval charges. It removes the need to guess.
rationales: Custom and costly to run; Intelligent-Tiering already does this.

Unpredictable access to archived data adds restore delays and retrieval costs.
Less resilient, and retrieval fees apply to unpredictable access.

questions.stem:
A company must keep application logs for 7 years. Logs are queried often for 30 days, occasionally for up to 1 year, and almost never after that. Each daily log batch is written as a few large compressed objects.

Which S3 Lifecycle configuration is most cost-effective?
options: Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering with no expiration.
Keep logs in S3 Standard for 30 days, transition to S3 Standard-IA, transition to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year, and expire after 7 years.
Keep all logs in S3 Standard for 7 years.
Write logs directly to S3 Glacier Deep Archive on day one.
questions.explanation: With a known, age-based access pattern and a few large objects, explicit Lifecycle transitions put data in the cheapest suitable tier at each stage. Expiration enforces the 7-year retention.
rationales: Workable, but retention is never enforced, and the access pattern is already known, so explicit rules fit better.
Correct. Each tier matches the known access pattern, and expiry enforces retention.
Overpays for years of rarely accessed data.
Frequent queries in the first 30 days would need slow, costly restores.

sources.title: S3 Lifecycle — S3 docs
S3 storage classes — S3 docs

questions.stem:
Cost analysis shows large spend on gp2 EBS volumes that were oversized only to get more IOPS. The volumes are attached to production instances that cannot have downtime.

Which action reduces cost without downtime?
options: Switch to st1 throughput-optimised HDD volumes.
Snapshot each volume, stop the instance and restore to io2.
Change the volumes to gp3 with Elastic Volumes, provisioning only the IOPS and throughput needed, and size capacity to actual usage on new volumes over time.
Detach the volumes and attach them to smaller instances.

Requires downtime and typically costs more.

Create an S3 gateway VPC endpoint and associate it with the private subnets' route tables.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration.

Enable Amazon Macie to classify resources by owner.
Create one VPC per business unit inside a single shared account.
Turn on detailed CloudWatch monitoring for all resources.

AWS Cost Anomaly Detection with a monitor on the account and an alert subscription.
AWS Trusted Advisor weekly email.

Convert all instances to Spot.
Move every instance to the next-smaller size without analysis.

Repurchase SaaS equivalents for each application
Replatform the workloads into containers on Amazon ECS
Relocate the VMs to VMware Cloud on AWS

Discovery data shows 60 on-premises servers averaging under 4% CPU and memory use for the last 90 days. Most have no inbound connections, and several have no named owner.

What should the migration team do with these servers first?

Rehost them to the smallest EC2 instance types to cut cost
Retain them on premises until the end of the migration
Confirm with business stakeholders and plan to retire them

rationales: Refactoring is the most expensive strategy and makes no sense for applications that may not be needed.
Moving unused servers still spends migration effort and running cost on systems nobody uses.

questions.stem:
A retailer must exit its data centre within 18 months. It has about 2,000 servers across 300 applications. The CIO also wants the company to become cloud-native and asks the architect for a migration approach.

Which approach best balances the deadline with the modernisation goal?
options: Pause migration until every application has a full code review and target cloud-native design
Repurchase SaaS products for all 300 applications to avoid migrating servers
Refactor all 300 applications into microservices before moving any of them so each moves only once
Rehost or replatform most applications in dependency-based waves to meet the exit date, then modernise high-value applications after they run in AWS

Refactoring is the slowest and costliest strategy, so applying it everywhere first would miss the exit date. Waves grouped by dependency limit cross-site latency during the move.
rationales: Blocking all moves on full redesigns guarantees a missed deadline.
SaaS replacements do not exist for every custom application, and a blanket repurchase ignores fit.
Refactoring 300 apps up front is the most complex path and is very unlikely to fit 18 months.
Correct. Migrate first in waves, then modernise selected workloads in AWS.

AWS Database Migration Service
AWS DataSync copying disk images to Amazon S3

questions.stem:
A team is using Application Migration Service (now AWS Transform MGN) to move an order-processing server. Replication shows healthy and continuous. The business has approved a two-hour cutover window tonight.

Which sequence gives the lowest risk of data loss during cutover?
options: Finalise the cutover first to free replication resources, then launch the cutover instance
Launch a test instance, promote it to production, and keep the source writing so you can fall back
Launch the cutover instance now, then stop the source application tonight and repoint DNS
During the window, stop writes on the source application, confirm replication has caught up, launch the cutover instance, validate it, repoint DNS, then finalise the cutover
questions.explanation: Writes must stop on the source before the final launch so the replicated disks contain every change. After validation and the DNS change, finalising the cutover cleans up replication. Launching early or keeping the source writing leaves changes behind.
rationales: Finalising first stops replication before you have a validated cutover instance.
With both systems writing, data diverges and the test instance is missing later writes.
Launching before writes stop means anything written afterwards never reaches the new instance.
Correct. Quiesce, let replication catch up, launch, validate, switch traffic, then finalise.

questions.stem:
A company is moving a 6 TB Oracle database with many PL/SQL procedures to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The application can be offline for no more than 30 minutes.

Which approach meets these requirements?
options: Replicate the database server with Application Migration Service, then change the engine on the EC2 instance
Use AWS DMS alone with a full load task; DMS converts the PL/SQL procedures automatically
Convert the schema and code with DMS Schema Conversion or AWS SCT, then use AWS DMS full load plus change data capture and cut over when lag is minimal
Export with Oracle Data Pump and import the dump file directly into Aurora PostgreSQL
questions.explanation: This is a heterogeneous migration, so the schema and code must be converted with DMS Schema Conversion or SCT; DMS itself moves data, not procedures. Full load plus CDC keeps Oracle live until a short cutover. Data Pump files cannot be loaded into PostgreSQL.
rationales: MGN rehosts the server as is; it does not convert Oracle to PostgreSQL.
DMS moves data only, and a full load alone without CDC would need a long outage.
Correct. Schema conversion first, then DMS full load and CDC for a short cutover.
Data Pump is an Oracle format and cannot be imported into PostgreSQL.

A media company has 300 TB on an on-premises NFS file server and a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect link. It must move the data to Amazon S3 within three weeks, keep users working during the copy, verify integrity, and run a short final sync at cutover.

Which solution should the architect recommend?
options: Deploy an AWS DataSync agent, schedule incremental tasks over Direct Connect to Amazon S3, and run a final task at cutover
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration and copy with the AWS CLI from one server
Deploy Amazon S3 File Gateway and let users write to it until all data is copied
Order AWS Snowball Edge devices and ship the data

A physical device is unnecessary at this bandwidth, and Snowball Edge has been closed to new customers since 2025-11-07.
rationales: Correct. DataSync over Direct Connect with scheduled incremental runs fits the time and integrity needs.
Transfer Acceleration targets long-distance internet uploads and offers no scheduling, incremental sync or verification.
A File Gateway changes how users work and does not migrate the existing 300 TB on its own.
The network can carry the data well within three weeks, so shipping devices adds delay and handling for no benefit; Snowball Edge is also closed to new customers.

Which solution meets these requirements?

Issue S3 presigned URLs and ask partners to upload with HTTPS
Run OpenSSH on an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances that mounts the S3 bucket
Create an AWS Transfer Family SFTP server that stores files in Amazon S3 and point the existing hostname at it

Correct. A managed SFTP endpoint backed by S3 with the same hostname keeps partners unchanged.

Request an AWS Snowmobile

Field teams on four continents upload multi-gigabyte video files to a single Amazon S3 bucket in us-east-1. Uploads from Asia and South America are slow, and the company wants the simplest change that improves upload speed.

What should the architect do?

Add more prefixes to the bucket to increase request throughput
Deploy an AWS DataSync agent on every field laptop
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket and have clients use the accelerate endpoint

questions.stem:
A company has rehosted a large Java monolith on Amazon EC2. It now wants to move features into independent services gradually, keep the application available throughout, and be able to roll back any single feature.

Which approach best meets these goals?
options: Move the monolith into a single large container and call it modernised
Freeze feature work, rewrite the whole application as microservices, and switch over in one release
Put an Application Load Balancer or Amazon API Gateway in front of the monolith and route individual paths to new services one at a time, each with its own data store
Split the monolith into services that all keep reading and writing the existing shared database

Giving each service its own data store avoids coupling through a shared database. A big-bang rewrite carries the highest risk.
rationales: Containerising the whole monolith changes packaging but does not split features.
A one-shot rewrite is the riskiest option and offers no gradual rollback.
Correct. This is the strangler fig pattern with per-route rollback.
A shared database keeps services tightly coupled and blocks independent changes.

questions.stem:
An order service calls an inventory service synchronously. During flash sales the inventory service slows down, order requests time out, and customers see errors even though orders could be processed a few seconds later.

Which change best improves resilience?
options: Move the inventory service to larger EC2 instances
Place an Amazon SQS queue between the services and scale inventory workers on queue depth
Publish orders to an Amazon SNS topic that the inventory service subscribes to over HTTPS
Use Route 53 weighted routing across two inventory endpoints
questions.explanation: An SQS queue absorbs bursts so the order service can accept requests immediately while inventory workers catch up. Scaling consumers on queue depth matches capacity to the backlog. SNS pushes to the subscriber and does not act as a buffer the subscriber drains at its own pace.
rationales: Bigger instances raise the ceiling but keep the synchronous coupling that causes timeouts.
Correct. A queue decouples the services and smooths spikes.
SNS pushes messages to the endpoint, which is still overwhelmed during spikes.
Weighted DNS spreads load but keeps the synchronous call and its timeouts.

questions.stem:
When an order is placed, billing, shipping and analytics must each receive the event, process it independently, retry on their own, and receive only the order types they care about.

Which TWO designs meet these requirements? (Select two.)
options: Publish to an Amazon EventBridge event bus with one rule per service that matches the needed order types and targets that service's SQS queue
Have the order service call billing, shipping and analytics REST APIs in sequence
Publish to an Amazon SNS topic with a separate Amazon SQS queue subscribed for each service, using subscription filter policies
Send each order to one Amazon SQS standard queue that all three services poll
questions.explanation: SNS-to-SQS fan-out and EventBridge rules targeting per-service queues both deliver every relevant event to each consumer, with filtering and an independent buffer and retry path for each. A single shared queue hands each message to only one consumer. Sequential REST calls couple the services and fail together.
rationales: Correct. EventBridge rules route by content to separate queues for each service.
Synchronous chained calls couple availability and do not give independent retries.
Correct. Fan-out with filter policies gives each service its own queue and filtering.
Each message in one queue is processed by only one consumer, so services miss events.

questions.stem:
A payments platform processes account transactions. Transactions for the same account must be handled in the order they were sent and must not be processed twice. Different accounts can be processed in parallel.

Which design meets these requirements?
options: An Amazon SQS FIFO queue using the account ID as the message group ID
An Amazon SNS standard topic with an HTTPS subscriber
An Amazon EventBridge rule with retries enabled
An Amazon SQS standard queue with a long visibility timeout
questions.explanation: SQS FIFO preserves order within a message group and removes duplicates. Using the account ID as the group keeps each account in order while different accounts run in parallel. Standard queues give at-least-once delivery with best-effort ordering.
rationales: Correct. FIFO ordering per message group with deduplication fits per-account order.
A standard SNS topic does not guarantee order or exactly-once handling.
EventBridge retries do not give ordered, deduplicated processing per account.
Standard queues do not guarantee order and can deliver duplicates, whatever the visibility timeout.

A company has 40 Java and .NET applications on Windows and Linux VMs. It wants to run them in containers on AWS without changing application code and without managing container hosts.

Which approach requires the least effort?
options: Build container images manually and run them on self-managed EC2 Docker hosts
Rewrite each application as AWS Lambda functions
Use AWS App2Container to generate container images and deployment artefacts, then run them on Amazon ECS or Amazon EKS with AWS Fargate
Rehost the VMs with Application Migration Service and install Docker on each EC2 instance by hand

Moving to Lambda is a refactor and requires code changes.
Correct. App2Container plus Fargate containerises without code changes or host management.

questions.stem:
A retailer stores shopping carts and user sessions in an on-premises Oracle database. Access is always by user ID, needs single-digit millisecond latency, and traffic can jump tenfold with no warning during promotions. The team wants minimal capacity planning.

Which target database is the best fit?

Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity
Amazon Redshift
Amazon Neptune

questions.stem:
An insurer wants to find fraud rings by following links between claims, people, addresses, phone numbers and bank accounts several hops deep. The current relational design needs many self-joins and is slow.

Which AWS database best fits this access pattern?

Amazon Neptune
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Amazon DynamoDB

OpenSearch is for search and log analytics, not graph traversal.
DynamoDB is key-value and document; multi-hop traversal would need many lookups.

Route S3 events through Amazon EventBridge to run an Amazon ECS task on AWS Fargate for each file
Keep the job on an EC2 instance with a cron schedule
Process the files with Lambda@Edge functions
